holidays.name: National Bean Day
holidays.description: A day for the humble legume. Think chili, baked beans, refried burritos and hummus. Beans are cheap and protein-packed, and they have a famously musical reputation. Pop culture fans also tip their hats to Mr. Bean on this day.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a fixture of the food-day calendar in the United States.
holidays.funFact: Gregor Mendel, the father of genetics, worked out his laws of inheritance by breeding pea plants. Peas are close cousins of the bean family, so the day doubles as a nod to legume science.

holidays.name: National Shortbread Day
holidays.description: A buttery, crumbly salute to the classic Scottish biscuit. All it takes is three humble ingredients: butter, sugar and flour. Pair it with tea and call it a holiday.
holidays.origin: Shortbread is a Scottish treat that grew out of medieval biscuit bread. It was refined into its buttery form over the centuries. The day is an unofficial observance that falls in the cozy stretch after the New Year.
holidays.funFact: Mary, Queen of Scots, is famously said to have loved a shortbread variety called Petticoat Tails. The name may come from the wedge shapes the dough is cut into.

holidays.name: National Cuddle Up Day
holidays.description: A day to snuggle under a blanket with a loved one, a pet or a very fluffy pillow. It arrives in the deep chill of winter, which is the perfect excuse to stay close and stay warm.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a winter tradition on the national day calendars.
holidays.funFact: Cuddling is linked to the release of oxytocin, often nicknamed the 'love hormone'. It can help people feel calmer and more connected.
